# -*- coding: utf-8 -*- """ User profile rendering module. This module provides a single function `render_user_profile` that takes user‑supplied data, sanitises it to prevent XSS and other injection attacks, and injects the cleaned values into a pre‑defined template. Security notes -------------- * All user inputs are passed through `html.escape` which neutralises any HTML or JavaScript that could be executed in a browser context. * The template is treated as read‑only; placeholders are replaced by the sanitized values only. * No external data is parsed or executed, mitigating CWE‑707 risks. """ from __future__ import annotations import html from typing import Final # Example template – in a real application this would be loaded from a file PROFILE_FORMAT: Final[str] = ( "
\n" "

{username}

\n" "

{biography}

\n" "
Status: {status}
\n" "
" ) def _sanitize(value: str) -> str: """ Escape a string for safe inclusion in HTML. Parameters ---------- value : str The raw user input. Returns ------- str A version of the string safe for HTML rendering. """ # html.escape replaces &, <, >, " and ' return html.escape(value, quote=True) def render_user_profile(username: str, biography: str, status: str) -> str: """ Construct a sanitized user profile HTML snippet. Parameters ---------- username : str The user's self‑provided name. biography : str A user‑authored biography that may contain multiple sentences. status : str A short, current status update submitted by the user. Returns ------- str The sanitized and formatted profile ready for web display. Raises ------ TypeError If any argument is not a string. """ # Basic type checking – helps prevent accidental injection of non‑string if not all(isinstance(arg, str) for arg in (username, biography, status)): raise TypeError("All arguments must be of type str") # Sanitize each component safe_username = _sanitize(username) safe_biography = _sanitize(biography) safe_status = _sanitize(status) # Render the final template rendered_profile = PROFILE_FORMAT.format( username=safe_username, biography=safe_biography, status=safe_status ) return rendered_profile # Example usage (for manual testing only) if __name__ == "__main__": sample = render_user_profile( "Alice ", "I love coding. Python is my favorite.", "Working on a new project!" ) print(sample)
